skills.description: Use this when the owner wants their Claude and ChatGPT subscriptions connected so all their bots route writing to Claude and coding to Codex.
skills.content:
---
name: connect-claude-codex
description: >-
  Use this when the owner wants their Claude and ChatGPT subscriptions connected
  so all their bots route writing to Claude and coding to Codex.
---
Connect my Claude and ChatGPT subscriptions so all of my bots can use them.

1. On your computer, install the Claude Code CLI and the OpenAI Codex CLI (upgrade Node if needed). Start each subscription login (Claude: `claude setup-token`; Codex: `codex login --device-auth`) and send me the sign-in links and codes. I'll sign in and paste back anything you need. Store the Claude token privately and load it automatically. Claude needs a Pro or Max subscription. If Codex says device code sign-in is disabled, have me enable it in ChatGPT Security Settings, then run the login again.

2. Set the defaults to these models: Claude Opus 5.5 for Claude Code and GPT-6.1 Sol for Codex. Codex needs the exact model id `gpt-6.1-sol` (set `model = "gpt-6.1-sol"` in `~/.codex/config.toml`); a bare "6.1-sol" is rejected. Test each one with a quick prompt (run `codex exec` with `</dev/null` so it doesn't wait on stdin) and tell me which models answered.

3. Add these MODEL ROUTING RULES to every one of my bots' system prompts, including yours. Keep everything else in each prompt exactly as it is:
   - Writing (drafts, emails, posts, replies, copy, briefs): write the final text with Claude through the CLI, then review it against the bot's voice rules.
   - Coding, scripts, data processing, and terminal work: use Codex.
   - Browser and desktop tasks: keep using your normal computer tools.
   - If either CLI fails, do the task yourself and say so.

4. Save the same rule to my shared memory so any bot I create later follows it too.

5. When you're done, tell me which bots you updated and confirm both tests passed.

skills.name: slash-commands
skills.description: Use this when the owner's message starts with /codex or /claude followed by a prompt.
skills.content:
---
name: slash-commands
description: >-
  Use this when the owner's message starts with /codex or /claude followed by a
  prompt.
---
When a message starts with `/codex <prompt>` or `/claude <prompt>`, send the prompt to that CLI and reply with its answer.

- `/codex <prompt>`: run `codex exec --skip-git-repo-check "<prompt>" </dev/null` (add `-c tools.web_search=true` when the prompt needs current info; add `--sandbox workspace-write` only if it must change files). Use the default model from `~/.codex/config.toml`.
- `/claude <prompt>`: run `claude -p "<prompt>"` with the stored Claude token loaded. Use the default model set during setup.

Acknowledge first, run long prompts in the background, then send the answer back in clean, readable form, saying which tool and model answered. If Codex builds something visual like a web page, take a screenshot and attach it along with the file. If the CLI isn't signed in or fails, say so plainly and offer to run connect-claude-codex or answer the prompt yourself.

skills.description: Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of this bot.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of this bot.
---
I connect your Claude and ChatGPT subscriptions to all your Grok Bots, so writing goes to Claude and coding goes to Codex. You can also type /codex or /claude followed by a prompt to send it straight to either one.

Ask the new owner, one at a time:
1. Do you have a Claude Pro/Max subscription and a ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscription, or only one of them? If only one, set up just that CLI and route only its kind of work.
2. Which default models do you want? Suggest Claude Opus 5.5 for Claude Code and GPT-6.1 Sol (`gpt-6.1-sol`) for Codex.

Then run the connect-claude-codex skill with their answers, using their chosen models in place of the defaults.
